title: Insulation Rebates in Halifax 2026: Attic, Walls, Basement
desc: Halifax insulation rebates for 2026: attic up to $750, walls up to $1,500, basement up to $1,200, air sealing $200, through Efficiency Nova Scotia. How row and semi homes are paid.
lead: Efficiency Nova Scotia pays Halifax homeowners for adding insulation and sealing air leaks, through its Home Energy Assessment. The amounts depend on where you insulate and how much of the area you cover. Townhouses and semis are paid at a lower rate for walls and foundations, which matters in a city with plenty of both.
cards_heading: What insulation rebates pay in Halifax
cards_intro: Amounts from Efficiency Nova Scotia's Home Energy Assessment rebate guide (August 2026), which its program page still links as of October 3, 2026. All of these are maximums, paid on the share of the area you insulate.

cards.title: Attic
cards.note: For bringing the attic up to R-50.

cards.title: Exterior walls
cards.note: Pro-rated by the share of wall area insulated.

cards.title: Air sealing
cards.note: Based on the air leakage measured at your final assessment.

cards.title: Moderate Income Rebate
cards.note: For homes heated mainly by non-electric fuel, under the income limits. Pre-approval required.

cards.title: HomeWarming
cards.note: Lower-income homeowners can get insulation and draft-proofing at no charge.

after_cards:
Semis and townhouses get less for walls

For wall and foundation insulation, Efficiency Nova Scotia pays semi-detached and end units 75% of the detached amount, and middle units 50%. So a middle townhouse that fully insulates its exterior walls gets up to $750 instead of $1,500. Attic rebates are not reduced this way. Halifax has about 12,460 semi-detached households and 7,490 in row houses, per the 2021 Census.
sections: Why insulation comes first in older Halifax homes

Statistics Canada's 2021 Census counted 85,640 Halifax households in homes built before 1981, about 45% of the total. Homes from that era were built before modern energy codes, and many still have thin attic insulation and uninsulated basement walls. Adding insulation lowers your heating bill whatever you heat with, and it lets a heat pump do its job with a smaller unit. That is why Efficiency Nova Scotia's assessment looks at the whole house, not just the furnace.

Newer Halifax homes are a different story. About 27% of households live in homes built since 2001. They usually start with decent insulation, so the payback on more is slower. The assessment will tell you whether it is worth doing.

You book an initial Home Energy Assessment ($199, waived for moderate-income households). An energy advisor checks your insulation, air leakage and heating system and leaves a report with recommended upgrades. You hire a contractor, do the work within 12 months, then book the final assessment. Rebates are paid after the final visit, up to $5,000 in total and never more than the work cost. The home must be at least six months old and the work must not have started before the first visit.

Insulating and sealing a home makes it tighter, which is the point. Efficiency Nova Scotia now reminds homeowners that tighter homes can change indoor air, including radon levels. Health Canada recommends every home be tested for radon. Some homes qualify for a free test kit through Lung NS-PEI. If you are finishing or insulating a basement, test first. A heat recovery ventilator (HRV) brings in fresh air without losing much heat, and Efficiency Nova Scotia pays $300 for one through the assessment.
claim_heading: How to get an insulation rebate in Halifax
claim_steps: Check if your income qualifies for HomeWarming (free) or the Moderate Income Rebate (needs pre-approval).
Book a Home Energy Assessment before any work starts.
Get quotes for the upgrades in your report, and ask each contractor what R-value and area they are covering.
Book the final assessment. Your rebate is calculated from what was actually added.
faq: How much is the insulation rebate in Halifax?

Up to $750 for the attic (to R-50), up to $1,500 for exterior walls, up to $1,200 for basement walls and up to $960 for a crawlspace, plus $200 for air sealing, through Efficiency Nova Scotia's Home Energy Assessment.
Do townhouses get the full insulation rebate?
Not for walls and foundations. End units and semis get 75% of the amount and middle units 50%. Attic rebates are not reduced.
Can I insulate first and apply later?
No. You need the initial assessment before the work starts, then a final assessment after. Work done before the first visit is not eligible.
Is there a free insulation program in Halifax?
Yes, for lower-income homeowners. HomeWarming covers insulation and draft-proofing at no charge. The after-tax income limit is $30,187 for one person and $57,075 for two to four people.
